_note: Curated context for the USD events that actually move gold. 'prior_move_usd' is a rough starting expectation only - it is superseded by the measured base rate in data/events.csv once that event has 3+ logged instances.

federal funds rate.name: FOMC Rate Decision
federal funds rate.what: The Federal Open Market Committee sets the target range for the federal funds rate. Announced at 19:00 UK (14:00 ET), followed 30 minutes later by the Chair's press conference.
federal funds rate.who: Federal Reserve, eight scheduled meetings a year
federal funds rate.why_gold: Gold pays no interest, so its opportunity cost is the real yield on cash and Treasuries. Anything that lowers expected real rates raises gold, and vice versa. This is the single most direct transmission channel there is.
federal funds rate.watch: The decision itself is usually priced in. The move comes from three other things: changes to the statement's language, the dot plot on projection meetings, and the tone of the press conference - which frequently reverses the initial statement reaction.
federal funds rate.gotchas: Two-leg event. Gold often moves one way on the 19:00 statement and the opposite way during the 19:30 presser. Judging the day on the first ten minutes is how people get caught.
federal funds rate.prior_move_usd: 20-60 on the day, more on projection meetings

fomc economic projections.name: Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot)
fomc economic projections.what: Every committee member's forecast for growth, unemployment, inflation and the appropriate policy rate. Published four times a year alongside the rate decision.
fomc economic projections.who: Federal Reserve, March / June / September / December
fomc economic projections.why_gold: The dot plot repriced the whole forward rate curve in one release. Gold trades the curve, not the current rate, so a shifted median dot moves it harder than the decision.
fomc economic projections.watch: The median dot for the current and next year, and how many members moved. The longer-run dot matters for the real-rate anchor.
fomc economic projections.gotchas: The dots are not a commitment and the Chair usually says so in the presser, which can unwind the initial move.

fomc meeting minutes.name: FOMC Meeting Minutes
fomc meeting minutes.what: Detailed account of the meeting held three weeks earlier. Released 19:00 UK.
fomc meeting minutes.who: Federal Reserve, three weeks after each meeting
fomc meeting minutes.why_gold: Reveals the spread of opinion behind a decision the market has already traded. Matters most when the vote looked closer than the statement implied.
fomc meeting minutes.watch: Phrases signalling how many members wanted a different outcome, and any discussion of the balance sheet.
fomc meeting minutes.gotchas: Stale by construction - if the data has moved since the meeting, the minutes are often ignored entirely.

cpi m/m.name: Consumer Price Index
cpi m/m.what: Headline and core consumer inflation, month on month and year on year. Released 13:30 UK (08:30 ET).
cpi m/m.who: Bureau of Labor Statistics, monthly, usually mid-month
cpi m/m.why_gold: The most reliable single driver of Fed expectations, and therefore of gold. A hot print lifts real yields and the dollar and knocks gold; a cool one does the reverse.
cpi m/m.watch: Core m/m is what the market trades - headline is noisier because of energy. A 0.1pp surprise against forecast is enough to move the metal.
cpi m/m.gotchas: Gold's first move is sometimes reversed within the hour if the internals (shelter, supercore) contradict the headline.

core pce price index.name: Core PCE Price Index
core pce price index.what: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, stripped of food and energy. Released 13:30 UK.
core pce price index.why_gold: It is the measure the Fed's 2% target is actually written against, so it carries more policy weight than CPI even though it moves markets less.
core pce price index.watch: The m/m figure to two decimal places, and the three- and six-month annualised runs that commentators compute from it.
core pce price index.gotchas: Largely predictable from the CPI and PPI released earlier in the month, so the surprise is usually small - which is exactly why a surprise here hits hard.

non-farm employment change.name: Non-Farm Payrolls
non-farm employment change.what: Net jobs added outside farming, plus the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings, all in one 13:30 UK release on the first Friday of the month.
non-farm employment change.why_gold: Labour market strength is the other half of the Fed's mandate. A strong report pushes rate-cut expectations out and pressures gold; a weak one brings cuts forward and supports it.
non-farm employment change.watch: Three numbers land simultaneously and can disagree: the payroll count, the unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings. Revisions to the prior two months often matter more than the headline.
non-farm employment change.gotchas: The most whipsaw-prone release on the calendar. The first move is frequently wrong, and the first fifteen minutes routinely reverse.

adp non-farm employment change.name: ADP Employment Change
adp non-farm employment change.what: Private payroll processor's estimate of job creation, released two days before NFP at 13:15 UK.
adp non-farm employment change.why_gold: Traded as a preview of NFP, though its correlation with the official number is poor.
adp non-farm employment change.watch: Only really matters when it diverges wildly from the NFP forecast.
adp non-farm employment change.gotchas: A bad predictor. Moves gold briefly, then gets forgotten by Friday.

benchmark payrolls revision.name: Benchmark Payrolls Revision
benchmark payrolls revision.what: Annual re-benchmarking of the payroll survey against actual tax records, which can rewrite a whole year of job growth in one line.
benchmark payrolls revision.who: Bureau of Labor Statistics, preliminary in late summer, final in February
benchmark payrolls revision.why_gold: A large downward revision means the labour market was weaker than the Fed thought all along, which is dovish and gold-positive.
benchmark payrolls revision.watch: The size of the revision against the prior year's figure. Six figures is a serious number.
benchmark payrolls revision.gotchas: Once-a-year event that most calendars underrate. It can reprice the whole rate path in a single print.

core ppi m/m.name: Producer Price Index
core ppi m/m.what: Inflation at the wholesale level, released 13:30 UK.
core ppi m/m.why_gold: A leading indicator for consumer inflation, and several PPI components feed straight into the PCE calculation, so analysts revise their PCE estimates within minutes of it.
core ppi m/m.watch: The health-care and portfolio-management components, because those are the ones that map into core PCE.
core ppi m/m.gotchas: Usually a minor event unless it lands the day before or after CPI.

core retail sales.name: Retail Sales
core retail sales.what: Monthly change in receipts at retail stores. Released 13:30 UK.
core retail sales.why_gold: The cleanest read on whether the consumer - roughly 70% of the US economy - is still spending. Feeds growth expectations and therefore the rate path.
core retail sales.watch: The control group, which strips autos, petrol, building materials and food services. That is the number that feeds GDP.
core retail sales.gotchas: Not adjusted for inflation, so a hot print during high inflation can mean less than it looks.

ism manufacturing pmi.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
ism manufacturing pmi.what: Survey of purchasing managers. Above 50 means expansion. Released 15:00 UK.
ism manufacturing pmi.who: Institute for Supply Management, first business day of the month
ism manufacturing pmi.why_gold: A timely growth signal that arrives before the hard data. Weakness feeds recession pricing, which is usually gold-supportive.
ism manufacturing pmi.watch: The prices-paid and new-orders sub-indices carry more information than the headline.
ism manufacturing pmi.gotchas: Manufacturing is a small share of US output, so the survey overstates its own importance.

ism services pmi.name: ISM Services PMI
ism services pmi.what: The services-sector equivalent, covering the bulk of the US economy. Released 15:00 UK.
ism services pmi.who: Institute for Supply Management, third business day of the month
ism services pmi.why_gold: More economically meaningful than the manufacturing survey and consequently a bigger mover when it surprises.
ism services pmi.watch: Prices paid, as a services-inflation signal, and employment as an NFP hint.
ism services pmi.gotchas: Noisier month to month than its manufacturing counterpart.

unemployment claims.name: Initial Jobless Claims
unemployment claims.what: New unemployment benefit filings in the prior week. Released every Thursday at 13:30 UK.
unemployment claims.why_gold: The highest-frequency labour signal available. Individually minor, but a trend of rising claims shifts the whole rate narrative.
unemployment claims.watch: The four-week moving average rather than the weekly print, and continuing claims for whether people are finding new work.
unemployment claims.gotchas: Distorted by holidays, weather and state-level administrative quirks. One bad week means nothing.

advance gdp q/q.name: GDP
advance gdp q/q.what: Quarterly economic growth, annualised. Released 13:30 UK in three passes - advance, second, third.
advance gdp q/q.why_gold: Matters for the growth half of the picture, but it is backward-looking by up to four months.
advance gdp q/q.watch: The advance reading is the only one that reliably moves anything. Later revisions rarely register.
advance gdp q/q.gotchas: Gold typically shrugs off GDP unless the miss is large or it confirms an existing recession narrative.

fed chair.name: Fed Chair Speaks
fed chair.what: Any scheduled appearance by the Fed Chair - testimony, conference remarks, or a moderated Q&A.
fed chair.why_gold: The Chair sets the policy narrative between meetings. A single sentence on the balance of risks can move the rate curve as much as a data release.
fed chair.watch: Whether the venue allows questions. Prepared remarks are usually safe; unscripted Q&A is where the surprises come from.
fed chair.gotchas: No forecast number exists, so nothing is priced in. The risk is pure tone, which makes it hard to hedge and easy to get run over by.

fomc member.name: FOMC Member Speaks
fomc member.what: Remarks from a regional Fed president or governor.
fomc member.why_gold: Mostly background, but a known hawk turning dovish - or the reverse - is a genuine signal, and voting members matter more than non-voters.
fomc member.watch: Whether the speaker votes this year, and whether they are departing from their usual stance.
fomc member.gotchas: Several speakers a day is normal and almost always noise. Treat as background unless the tone genuinely shifts.

treasury sec.name: Treasury Secretary Speaks
treasury sec.what: Remarks from the US Treasury Secretary.
treasury sec.why_gold: Moves gold through the dollar and through issuance expectations rather than through rates - comments on currency policy or debt supply are the ones that land.
treasury sec.watch: Anything on dollar policy, tariffs, or the debt issuance mix.

consumer confidence.name: CB Consumer Confidence
consumer confidence.what: Survey of household sentiment about business and labour conditions. Released 15:00 UK.
consumer confidence.why_gold: A soft indicator of future spending. Rarely moves gold on its own.
consumer confidence.watch: The labour differential - jobs plentiful minus jobs hard to get - which tracks the unemployment rate.
consumer confidence.gotchas: Sentiment surveys have decoupled from actual spending behaviour for years now.

uom consumer sentiment.name: UoM Consumer Sentiment
uom consumer sentiment.what: Michigan's household survey, released in preliminary and revised form at 15:00 UK.
uom consumer sentiment.why_gold: The sentiment number is minor. The inflation-expectations component attached to it is not.
uom consumer sentiment.watch: The 1-year and 5-10 year inflation expectations. The Fed watches the long-run figure closely, so a jump there is a genuine rate signal.
uom consumer sentiment.gotchas: Small sample, frequently revised, and prone to reflecting petrol prices more than anything else.

jolts job openings.name: JOLTS Job Openings
jolts job openings.what: Job openings, hires and quits. Released 15:00 UK, roughly six weeks in arrears.
jolts job openings.why_gold: The vacancy-to-unemployed ratio is a labour-tightness gauge the Fed has cited directly.
jolts job openings.watch: The quits rate, as a measure of worker confidence.
jolts job openings.gotchas: Very stale by release, and the response rate has been falling for years.
